answer: Sybil resistance in the agent economy rests on a stake-bonded identity ledge: every agent must lock a bond before its key can vote or claim rewards, and each bond is bound to one human-verified root. Launching a thousand fake agents means financing a thousand separate bonds, so attacker cost scales linearly with identity count while payout per identity stays flat, and the tide of cheap accounts turns expensive. A verifier who proves an identity is duplicated seizes the entire bond and takes a share of that nectar, so forged agents subsidize honest challengers instead of earning profit.
